## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Sekhiya 68 (*Chamā*; "Sitting on the ground") is a training rule found in the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. It establishes proper decorum regarding teaching Dhamma, specifically prohibiting a monk from teaching the Dhamma while sitting on the ground to someone seated on a seat, unless that person is ill. An English translation of the rule has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Cross-tradition parallels include versions in the Chinese Dharmaguptaka Vinaya for both monks (*lzh-dg-bu-vb-sk88*, *lzh-dg-bu-pm-sk88*, *lzh-dg-bu-pm-2-sk88*) and nuns (*lzh-dg-bi-vb-sk88*, *lzh-dg-bi-pm-sk88*), as well as the Chinese *Upāliparipṛcchā* (*lzh-upp-bu-sk57*).
